title: how the sitemap gets its lastmod dates
summary: The sitemap's <lastmod> values are not produced by Astro or by the deploy workflow alone — they come from git history read at build time, so the correctness of every date depends on a setting in a DIFFERENT file: actions/checkout's fetch-depth in .github/workflows/pages.yml. A shallow clone does not make git log fail; it answers every path with the single commit it has, so per-file dates come back uniform and wrong rather than absent. That is why astro.config.mjs probes `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` up front and emits NO lastmod at all when history is unusable: a wrong lastmod on every URL is worse than none, because it trains Google to ignore the field.

steps.role: fetch-depth: 0 makes full git history available to the build; removing it silently disables lastmod
maps each route to its source file and stamps that file's last-commit date, guarded on clone depth

invariants: fetch-depth: 0 in pages.yml is load-bearing for lastmod, not an optimisation
lastmod is omitted entirely rather than faked when git history is unusable
blog posts stamp from their markdown in src/content/blog, never from [slug].astro, so template edits do not restamp every post
